memory_update.text: No clean US-listed pure-play equivalent was identified for the highest-scarcity materials named in the provided evidence: Ajinomoto build-up film and MEC copper-adhesion surface chemistry. Treat US-listed names as adjacent proxies unless direct supplier/customer evidence emerges.
AMKR is a second-order advanced-packaging capacity proxy for the FC-BGA/AI accelerator package node, but evidence must separate AI/HPC advanced-packaging exposure from broader OSAT cyclicality.
ONTO is a plausible underfollowed yield-control proxy because it explicitly targets advanced IC substrates, panel-level packaging, and AI/HPC applications with inspection/metrology tools.

CAMT is a plausible mid-cap advanced-packaging inspection/metrology proxy with explicit HBM and heterogeneous-integration order evidence, but customer concentration and order cyclicality require verification.

For US-listed equities, the node maps better to advanced-packaging yield-control tools and capacity infrastructure than to direct ownership of the scarce insulating film or copper surface-chemistry suppliers.

node: HBM and AI accelerator advanced-package substrates, insulating films, and surface chemistry
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the AI accelerator advanced-packaging substrate node. The cleanest pure-play bottleneck names cited in the provided evidence are not normal US-listed investable equities: Ajinomoto for build-up film, MEC Company for copper adhesion chemistry, and Asian substrate makers such as Ibiden, Unimicron, Kinsus, AT&S, and Shinko. Within US-listed equities, the most plausible mapping shifts to adjacent chokepoints: advanced packaging capacity, panel or substrate inspection and metrology, and 2.5D/3D AI package yield-control equipment. This pass keeps TSM as the reference demand/capacity anchor and prioritizes AMKR, ONTO, and CAMT as underfollowed or less-obvious public-market proxies. No buy/sell recommendation is made.
